chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A time will come upon people when it will be harsh; each person will bite (cling greedily) to what is in his hand, and they will forget generosity/bounty, although Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has said, 'And do not forget generosity/bounty among yourselves.' Then a group of people will rise up in that time, buying out the needy/those in distress; those are the worst of people.

key_terms.وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ: And do not forget generosity among yourselves (Quranic quote)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the behavior of people and the worst of them during times of economic hardship?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) foretells a period of economic scarcity where hoarding becomes prevalent, causing the virtue of generosity (*al-fadl*) to be forgotten. He specifically identifies those who capitalize on the distress of the poor—effectively engaging in exploitative practices—as the 'worst of people,' linking this moral decay to the Quranic command to remember kindness. This narration serves as a critical ethical guideline for merchants, warning against opportunistic exploitation during crises.
